H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a flat gate-control sequence: arrival detection, close to 45 degrees, obstacle check, close to 90 degrees, departure-triggered opening.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Meaningful guards include IR-1 train arrival, 45-degree check point, pressure-switch obstacle presence/absence, and IR-2 departure detection.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include anticlockwise motor closing, clockwise motor opening, stopping the motor at 45 degrees, and activating the emergency light/signal.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: If a vehicle is detected at the 45-degree check, the controller stops the motor and sends an emergency signal to the train driver.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Core behavior is split across introduction, proposed implementation/algorithm, and results sections; D1 emergency-light behavior appears in the results rather than the algorithm.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as anti-collision and emergency signal are used, but the relevant stop-and-alert behavior is explicitly stated in the paper.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Motor directions and emergency-light actions are described in narrative result prose, requiring attribution back to arrival, departure, and obstacle cases.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper provides sequential checks over train sensor, gate angle, and pressure switch, but no explicit combined arithmetic or boolean guard expression.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state with its own entry, during, or exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Obstacle handling is tied to the 45-degree closing check, not declared as a from-any-state recovery rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The 45-degree clear-versus-obstacle branch gives weak benefit from explicit guard representation, but there are not three or more arithmetic/boolean guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting rule applies to multiple substates, and no parent-level continuous monitor is declared.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The emergency indication to the train driver is partly abstract, although the implementation also grounds it as LED D1.

key_nl_quotes: When the gate is closing down it will stop and check at 45 degrees for any presence of the vehicle.
Microcontroller will give signal to the motor to Stop and send this emergency signal to the train driver.
one_line_pitch: A compact railway-gate EFSM whose stress comes from sensor-guarded 45-degree branching, motor/emergency side effects, and cross-section action attribution.
rationale: This is a valid EFSM sample with clear guarded branching, nontrivial actuator outputs, and a dedicated obstacle emergency path. It is weaker as a top stress-test because it has no hierarchy, no global escape rule, and no documented complex arithmetic guard. Its main benchmark value is as a backup case for action attribution and simple but safety-relevant guard modeling.
